tasks.task: Write a data dictionary for files, CRM fields or tables

items.when: When each column needs a plain meaning, type, allowed values, example and owner
Before writing meanings, to see each column's shape, missing values and odd entries
When one important table needs a fuller entry with sources and who may use it
When a column is worked out by a query and you must say what it really counts
When the dictionary comes from a database schema and the links should be drawn

tasks.task: Write a business glossary the whole team uses

items.when: When terms like active customer or booking need one agreed meaning
When the terms are still argued over, to talk them through and record each decision
When a term is a metric and needs its exact working written down
When a definition sounds clear, to try it against hard cases before it is agreed

tasks.task: Set naming and pick-list rules for a CRM or shared sheets

items.when: When each field needs its valid values and format written as a rule you can check
When the same field lives in two tools, to set which one owns it
When pick-lists should be enforced with dropdowns on the sheet itself
When rules exist, to list CRM records with missing fields, stale dates and mismatches

tasks.task: Note where each report's numbers come from

items.when: When each source table behind a report needs its meaning and quality notes
When two reports use one name for different counts and need a worked comparison
When a number differs between two reports, to find the step where they split
When a recurring report may have changed its definition without anyone saying

tasks.task: Write data quality rules and the checks that run them

items.when: When a dataset needs rules for complete, valid, unique, consistent, linked and fresh
Before writing rules, to find the gaps, duplicates and odd values already there
When a rule must run as a query on the client's database
When you need a file of bad rows to prove each check fires
When checks keep catching the same fault, to fix where the record is made

tasks.task: Run the weekly data quality check

items.when: Weekly before reports, and straight after a new import, form or integration
When the week's results should be one scorecard per dataset
When failed rows should be fixed and rechecked until the file passes
When checks should alert only on unusual change, with baselines and quiet periods

tasks.task: Check a file before it goes into a system

items.when: Before a CSV goes into a CRM, stock, booking or accounts system
When spacing, numbers stored as text and mixed dates must be fixed first
When characters or dates break on import, to read and save the file correctly
When the file must be matched to records already held, to find doubles and orphans

tasks.task: Audit CRM data and write a change table

items.when: When the export needs profiling, rules and a table of proposed changes
When deals and contacts need a fix list that changes nothing by itself
When lead source fields may be too poor to link leads to campaigns
When records miss company or contact details the team relies on

tasks.task: Find duplicates and write a merge plan

items.when: When customers, companies or products are doubled and need keys, review and a plan
When records span several tools, to compare a second matching and scoring design
When the records are a Shopify store's customers
When a Shopify store's products share a code or barcode
Before any merge runs, to get a named person's sign-off on the review list

tasks.task: Build made-up test, demo or training data

items.when: When data must match the client's columns, types and rules without real people in it
Before building, to list the awkward cases the data must contain
When you want a second, differently built file as CSV, JSON, SQL or a script
When a new database needs realistic, repeatable seed data loaded

tasks.task: Write test cases that use the test data

items.when: When each import or form path needs a starting state, steps and expected result
When you must decide which cases matter, smallest first
When each case needs its own rows with the expected outcome marked

tasks.task: Map every old field to a new one before data moves

items.when: When moving from spreadsheets or an old system and nothing is mapped yet
When each column needs a target, a rule, open gaps and decisions to review
When the map is one part of a wider move that also needs checks and a rollback path

tasks.task: Write the transform and clean-up rules for a move

items.when: When the rules should follow from the agreed field map
When many rows need a few tested fix rules, a change log and a risky-row list
When missing values, wrong types and outliers must be fixed before loading

tasks.task: Plan a system move with a test import and record counts

items.when: When switching CRM, accounts, booking or till and no record may be lost
When the move needs field maps, checks and a rollback path in one plan
When the old system must stay live during the move, to compare a staged plan
When old and new tables are in SQL Server and must be proved to match

tasks.task: Write the cut-over checklist with rollback steps

items.when: When the rollout needs launch checks, open blockers and a decision record
When the day itself needs checks, a rollback plan and a sign it worked
When several parts switch at once, to find the joins where things can fall through
Before the switch, to confirm a backup exists and a restore has been tried
When staff must change how they work, to plan messages and handle pushback
When the plan assumes nothing goes wrong, to walk each handoff and human slip

tasks.task: Write tests and a contract for a model that feeds reports

items.when: When a model feeds reports or other teams and needs tests and freshness checks
When the model carries a metric whose working must be fixed first
Before the model is relied on, to find wrong-result risks in its SQL

tasks.task: Log a data issue and find its root cause

items.when: When a check fails or a report is wrong and the fix should be at the source
When the issue keeps coming back and needs a chain of whys checked against facts
When the issue hurt a report or customer and needs a blame-free write-up
When the fix should change a procedure and leave tracked prevention actions

tasks.task: Trace a correction request across every copy of a record

items.when: When someone says their details are wrong and every copy must be found and fixed
When nobody knows where personal data lives, to map it across systems
When the person is owed a reply, to draft it with the steps taken
When the request touches privacy law, to check duties and the proof you lack

tasks.task: Set rules for new uses of customer data

items.when: When a team wants to use customer data in a new way and needs a review before launch
When a data plan may no longer match the published privacy policy

tasks.task: Report data quality to managers

items.when: When managers want one score per dataset and the trend
When the trend in failed checks should be shown as a clean chart
When the report must be one page with the decision needed first

tasks.task: Document a dataset so its analysis can be repeated

items.when: When someone else must repeat an analysis from a data inventory and method notes
When every assumption should be logged with its risk for reviewers

tasks.task: Strip personal details before data is shared or used for tests

items.when: When a pile of text or files must have copies, junk and personal details removed
When names or numbers in a PDF must be redacted with the original kept safe
When made-up data would do the job and no real record needs to leave the system

always.when: Before any work, when the system, the columns or the use of the data is not stated
Before a dictionary or rules sheet is handed over, to catch a term used two ways

helpers.when: When checks must run inside a pipeline or warehouse, or loads need a run book
When records must be re-keyed or a batch of documents entered to the new rules
When retention, access or privacy duties decide what may be kept or merged
When the test data feeds a full test plan for an app or integration
When metric definitions and dashboards must be rebuilt on the cleaned data
When CRM stages, owners and routing must change, not only the data in them

gaps: No library item writes a whole data dictionary with allowed values and owners, or builds one from a database schema; only single-table entries
No library item sets naming and pick-list rules for a CRM or shared sheets
No library item writes data quality checks as SQL for a named database (nulls, uniqueness, broken links, freshness)
No library item plans fuzzy matching, which record survives and a merge order; the duplicate finders are for Shopify only
No library item plans a test import with record counts and proves old and new systems match, except for SQL Server tables
No library item sets data owners, stewards, access levels or a retention schedule for a small firm
No library item keeps a data quality issue log with severity, owner and status
No library item traces one person's record across every system for a correction request
No library item writes dbt tests, freshness checks or model contracts; only the kit prompt does
No library item masks or scrambles real data to make safe test data
